A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniREditBench, UniREdit-Data-100K, and UniREdit-Bagel. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniREdit-Bagel training and evaluation results on UniREditBench, RISEBench, and KRISBench, including quantitative tables and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and adds human evaluation, reference ablations, transfer experiments, CoT assessments, and training-data scaling results.

M1.justification: The synthesis pipeline, Bagel fine-tuning procedure, reasoning-text and flow-matching objectives, and dual-reference scoring formula remain unchanged. Newly specified loss coefficients and empirical support for the existing scoring weights do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,700-example benchmark, 100,421-example training dataset, eight primary dimensions, eighteen categories, and RISEBench/KRISBench evaluations. The additional studies use retained coverage; the expanded game-rule descriptions do not establish newly introduced tasks.

E2.justification: v3 substantially expands the UniREditBench comparison by adding Bagel, Lumina-DiMOO, DreamOmni2, and UniWorld-V2 to Tables 2 and 7. Bagel already appeared in v1's RISEBench comparison, but its participation in the in-domain comparison is new. The existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a six-expert study of 200 randomly selected samples across four models, MAE-based evaluator validation, alternative reference settings, Qwen3VL-32B-Instruct evaluation, Gemini-3-Pro binary CoT assessment, and training-data ablation/scaling settings. The KRISBench evaluator designation also changes from GPT-4.1 in v1 Table 4 to GPT-4o in v3 Table 6, although identical numbers do not establish that this experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v1 lacks the systematic validation and ablations introduced in v3 Section 5.4 and Appendices B and F–I. These examine human–VLM agreement, omission of either reference modality, scoring weights, evaluator dependence, game-to-real transfer, CoT causality/alignment, and performance as training data increases from 20K to 100K.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix B/Table 5 adds estimated Pearson correlations between human judgments and GPT-4.1 scores under six weighting schemes, providing a limited addition of correlation statistics. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new analyses remain point estimates.

E6.justification: The retained GPT-4.1 UniREditBench tables revise many scores: UniREdit-Bagel's overall score changes from 78.87 to 78.15 and GPT-4o's from 71.64 to 73.39. v3 also adds baseline rows and substantial validation/analysis results, including real-world averages of 73.81 without game data versus 75.74 with it, and CoT scores of 0.99 and 0.84. RISEBench and KRISBench numerical results are retained. The PDFs do not explain the cause of the revised in-domain scores.

T1.justification: The scoring equations and training-loss formulations are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The added game rules and empirical correlation analysis provide task documentation and evaluation evidence rather than new theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: broader reasoning coverage, dual-reference evaluation, a synthetic CoT-annotated training dataset, and improved editing through Bagel fine-tuning. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets game-data inclusion as positive transfer to real-world editing. Appendix K also characterizes previously displayed gem deletion and box duplication as 'Logical Hallucination,' connecting them to object permanence, conservation, and state consistency. These extend the existing interpretation of reasoning failures without changing the paper's overall account.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility documentation through Appendix L's operational rules for all nine game categories, including coordinates, movement, projections, scoring, puzzle variants, and move-selection priorities. It also specifies loss weights of 2 and 1 and adds the human-evaluation interface. These are newly documented details; the PDFs do not establish corresponding changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including FreeInpaint, ControlThinker, CompBench, ImagDressing-v1, ImagPose, and ComplexBench-Edit, while removing the sentence-embedding and Game-RL bibliography entries. Expanded Table 1 and Appendix A distinguish reference modalities, explicit rules, action control, and intra-game tasks. The central positioning relative to earlier editing benchmarks remains intact.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence are retained, with grammatical refinements, updated authorship/affiliation text, and modest explanatory edits. v3 adds Section 5.4 and reorganizes the appendix around the new analyses, but does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of existing displays. Table 1 gains comparison columns, benchmark tables gain rows and revised styling, and v3 adds validation/ablation tables, reference and scaling plots, and a human-evaluation interface figure. Existing qualitative comparisons are largely retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v1's central evaluation-reliability claim relied chiefly on qualitative illustration. v3 adds direct human validation and reference ablations in Section 5.4, addressing an important evidential gap, while transfer, scaling, evaluator comparisons, and explicit game rules strengthen validation and reproducibility. Reporting remains imperfect: Section 5.3 retains the old +17.08 game-world margin although revised Table 2 implies 18.41, and uncertainty estimates remain absent. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
